headline: Hallmark Gives AI Interfaces A Visual Brief
lede: Hallmark turns AI-assisted web building into a directed design process, pairing 48 material-based themes with real imagery, responsive checks, and accessibility gates. It helps agents escape the familiar grammar of generic gradients, card grids, and mechanically composed pages.

headline: TradingAgents Builds A Debate-Driven Market Desk
lede: TradingAgents assembles analysts, debaters, traders, and risk managers into a graph-coordinated research workflow. Checkpointed runs, persistent logs, parallel processing, and backtesting give the system a repeatable frame for studying machine-assisted decisions without confusing simulation for advice.

headline: ThinkRail Gives Coding Agents A Proper Workbench
lede: ThinkRail places autonomous coding inside the familiar discipline of branches, worktrees, reviews, CI, and merges. Isolated workspaces let several agent tasks advance in parallel while durable specifications and shared tooling keep the project legible.

headline: Cindy Turns Agents Into A Local Operator
lede: Cindy gives an assistant access to files, applications, browsers, phones, and connected tools while keeping the orchestration open and configurable. Local execution, interchangeable harnesses, shared memory, and optional hosted services put control over credentials and context back in the operator’s hands.

headline: ECC Turns Coding Assistants Into Engineering Crews
lede: ECC replaces one-shot prompting with a plan, test, implement, review, verify, and remember loop. Its agents, skills, hooks, commands, and persistent instincts give terminal-based coding assistants a rugged operating procedure, while AgentShield checks the machinery for dangerous permissions and prompts.

headline: Impeccable Teaches Coding Agents To Notice Design
lede: Impeccable gives frontend agents a working vocabulary for typography, layout, motion, accessibility, and polish. Deterministic detectors and targeted commands turn vague visual dissatisfaction into inspectable problems that can be iterated in the browser.

headline: SkillSpector Inspects Agents Before They Run
lede: SkillSpector treats agent skills as executable supply-chain inputs, scanning repositories, archives, files, and MCP snapshots for 71 patterns across 17 risk categories. Risk scores, OSV lookups, baselines, and SARIF reports give teams a practical gate before granting third-party skills access.

headline: Microduck Carries Learned Locomotion Into Hardware
lede: Microduck is a complete path from reinforcement-learning simulation to a 25-centimeter bipedal robot that walks, kicks, rolls, and streams its surroundings. Rust daemons, a 50 Hz control loop, verified updates, and rollback support make the tiny duck a serious embedded systems study.

headline: OpenBot Keeps AI Teammates On The Night Shift
lede: OpenBot gives persistent agents their own workspaces, queues, conversations, and channels, allowing long-running tasks to continue without a maze of open windows. Local storage, self-hosting, browser control, and automatic context compaction make it a quiet operations room for parallel machine work.

headline: Agent Reach Routes The Open Web Around Friction
lede: Agent Reach builds a capability layer for live web research, dispatching requests across open backends for GitHub, YouTube, Reddit, and social platforms. Primary routes, automatic fallbacks, local credentials, and browser-aware configuration turn brittle platform access into a maintained data stream.
